summary:
Medium read-only reconnaissance complete. The repository already has a fail-closed KMS wire/service foundation and an opaque KMS-DH adapter, but neither a usable root provider nor a client mTLS stack. Silo is a distinct, older raw IPC prototype whose current service is non-operational as shipped (`silo-guest.bin` is 0 bytes), accepts requests from any cell, and is incompatible with ADR-0005’s service-net-only authorization boundary. The existing real board (RPi3) must not be a Silo production target: its current Cellos lane runs at EL1, while the in-tree Silo needs EL2/Stage-2. QEMU/host evidence can establish software contracts only; a production provider must be separately hardware-qualified and cannot be selectable accidentally.

Exact evidence / incomplete behavior:
- `docs/decisions/0005-mutual-tls-relay-identity.md:16-23, 81-98, 130-169` (authoritative) requires TLS 1.3 mTLS only, no raw/K1 fallback, protected P-256 `CertificateVerify`, service-net-attested signing authorization, no exported private bytes, and two-node opaque-Noise evidence. It explicitly calls the client blocked.
- `cells/services/kms/src/dispatch.rs:23-55, 103-158` is the KMS public dispatcher. Registration/status work; `AcquireNodeIdentity`, valid `NoiseStaticDh`, and `RotateNodeIdentity` deliberately return `SecureRootRequired` after authorization/metadata validation. There is no signing operation for TLS.
- `cells/services/kms/src/storage.rs:43-45` hardwires `runtime_root()` to `UnavailableRootProvider`; `storage/provider.rs:39-50` is the single existing `RootProvider` seam; `storage/root.rs:30-130` provides strong fail-closed readiness gates (provider type, sealed epoch, rollback, anti-rollback, production capability, measurement, device binding, journal consistency). No non-test provider implementation exists.
- `cells/services/kms/src/auth.rs:19-83` uses kernel caller trailers plus current NET_BROKER/SUPERVISOR TID lookup. It authorizes broker generation binding and supervisor rotation; it has no service-net signer authorization model. `cells/services/kms/src/main.rs:19-39` receives through `sys_recv_attested`, parses the trailer, and supplies those two registry entries.
- `libs/types/src/kms/model.rs:26-105` freezes the v1 opcode and result vocabulary; `libs/types/src/kms/payload/binding.rs:83-128` and `payload/noise.rs:7-78` define opaque identity/DH payloads. `libs/ostd/src/clients/kms.rs:26-161` is the synchronous public KMS client; its constant request ID and single receive are acceptable only for serialized use.
- `cells/services/net-broker/src/kms_dh.rs:27-147` is the correct no-private-scalar direction: `OpaqueStaticKey` serializes only tag/handle/binding epoch/public key, and device-side static DH asks KMS. It fails closed off target OS. However `cells/services/net-broker/src/main.rs:108-110` still generates a per-boot local `StaticKeypair`; no KMS registration/status/acquire path constructs an opaque static identity today.
- `cells/services/net-broker/src/connection_manager.rs:6-7, 39-71` correctly has no relay fallback: direct Noise exhaustion returns `NotSupported`. `docs/project-roadmap.md:156-165` reports the same current state.
- `cells/services/net/src/tls.rs:1-16`, `tls/provider.rs:1-50`, `tls/socket.rs:7-37`, and `libs/ostd/src/clients/tls_stream.rs:27-34` implement server-authenticated TLS only: pinned CA plus hostname verification is available; no client chain, TLS client-auth profile, signing-key trait adapter, KMS call, or protected signer exists. Raw TLS IPC (`tls_wire.rs:7-103`, `tls_handler.rs:41-192`) has only connect/send/recv/close.
- `cells/services/silo/src/main.rs:8-27, 54-114` embeds a zero-byte guest and returns before service loop. It also calls `run_until_done` expecting initial `SILO_READY` without first sending `Init`; guest code actually waits for an Init mailbox command (`cells/guests/silo-guest/src/main.rs:45-111`). Thus even a manually copied guest binary does not establish an automatic durable seed/root lifecycle.
- `cells/services/silo/src/ipc.rs:51-143` uses unauthenticated `sys_recv(0)` from any cell and forwards raw Sign/Ecdh/GetPub, contrary to the required KMS-owned, service-net-only signing boundary. `libs/ostd/src/silo.rs:67-211` exposes public `init_key`, `sign`, and `ecdh` directly to arbitrary callers; `cells/tests/silo-test/src/main.rs:1-270` deliberately exercises that model with deterministic `[0x42; 32]` seeding. It is development/test evidence, not production custody evidence.
- `cells/guests/silo-guest/src/crypto.rs:20-164` does keep its `SigningKey` internal and zeroes the received seed stack buffer, but it uses P-256 ECDSA/static P-256 ECDH—not the KMS C2C X25519 contract—and shared host/guest mailbox plus Stage-2 are not a hardware root of trust by themselves.
- `kernel/src/task/cap.rs:246-276` grants HypervisorCap only if manifest plus EL2/H-ext/x86 root capability are present. `kernel/src/hypervisor/registry.rs:83-248` implements ARM Stage-2 only under `target_arch=aarch64` (x86 delegates to a separate SVM registry); `kernel/src/task/syscall.rs:5077-5120` gates VM syscalls on that cap. `kernel/src/loader/boot_ceiling.rs:98-105` permits `/bin/silo` to request it, but this is an execution-capability gate, not hardware-root attestation.
- `libs/api/src/abi/caller_identity.rs:11-66, 68-136` and `libs/ostd/src/syscall.rs:1038-1089` provide the correct unforgeable caller identity trailer mechanism. It is the boundary to reuse for service-net-only KMS signing authorization.

Test conventions and evidence status:
- KMS unit tests are colocated: `cells/services/kms/src/tests.rs`, `src/tests/authorization.rs`, `src/tests/operations.rs`; they construct fixed 128-byte requests, synthetic caller identity, and registry snapshots, asserting typed fail-closed errors.
- KMS wire tests are colocated under `libs/types/src/kms/tests.rs`, testing frozen sizes, canonical parsing, and payload round-trips. `net-broker/src/kms_dh/tests.rs` validates opaque representation and host fail-closure; it does not invoke real KMS.
- service-net tests currently cover parser/socket ownership behavior (`cells/services/net/src/tls_wire/tests.rs`, `handlers/tests.rs`, `socket_table/tests.rs`), not an mTLS handshake/signing path.
- Silo has no host crypto unit-test module; its only relevant executable evidence is the manually seeded `silo-test` Cell. No test was run because this assignment is explicitly read-only with no tests/builds.

Documentation conflicts/staleness requiring correction in the implementation plan:
- `docs/guides/tier1-silo.md:16, 191-195, 247-251` describes QEMU ARM64 Silo support and “secure isolated EL2 context” too broadly; it does not disclose the checked-in zero-byte guest, missing automatic initialization, absent durable seed/anti-rollback lifecycle, or lack of service-net authorization.
- `cells/services/silo/src/run_loop.rs:1-4` says the guest “boots, generates a P-256 key,” while `cells/guests/silo-guest/src/main.rs:81-91` requires host-sent Init seed. This is a source-comment contradiction.
- `docs/project-changelog.md:3213-3229` historical wording claims Silo end-to-end cases passed; it must be explicitly labeled historical development/QEMU-style evidence, not evidence of a current deployable protected root.
- `research/research-cell-security-permissions.md:151` calls Stage-2 Silo a software approximation and recommends external OpenTitan backing; that is directionally compatible with ADR-0005, whereas `docs/guides/tier1-silo.md` overstates protection.
- `docs/project-roadmap.md:156-165`, `docs/roadmap/current-focus.md:21-23`, and ADR-0005 are current and correctly say remote operation/client mTLS remain blocked. They should remain the status authority.

files.description: Authoritative architecture and acceptance criteria; locks mTLS-only relay, service-net-authorized protected P-256 signer, no private-key export, and no raw/K1 fallback.
KMS runtime, attested authorization, sole root-provider seam, and fail-closed readiness assessment. Runtime provider is intentionally unavailable.
Frozen fixed-frame KMS ABI v1 and opaque identity/DH data contracts; extending this is a public ABI decision.
Current public synchronous KMS client contract; basis for new protected signer operations once KMS ABI/provider supports them.
Kernel-written caller identity trailer contract required for attested service-net authorization.
Opaque KMS DH adapter exists but is unwired; broker still creates per-boot static key; relay fallback intentionally returns NotSupported.
Current server-auth TLS-only provider and raw IPC interface; lacks client cert, protected signer, and mTLS profile.
Public TLS stream explicitly documents it cannot reach the mutual-TLS relay.
Legacy Silo service: zero-byte embedded guest, missing init flow, all-caller raw IPC, and Stage-2 VMM wrapper.
Bare-metal P-256 guest implementation; private scalar is internal but key initialization is caller-supplied and not a production root lifecycle.
Legacy all-caller SiloHandle API; must not be the production relay authorization boundary.
Development Silo T1–T6 executable convention; deterministic seed and raw API demonstrate why it cannot qualify a production root.
Hypervisor capability, VM syscall gate, Stage-2 registry, and launch ceiling ownership.
Current truthful relay-client blocked status and no-fallback behavior.
Stale/overbroad Silo security and QEMU support claims needing qualified-evidence wording.

architecture:
Dependency graph and safest KISS phase ordering:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  B[net-broker direct Noise] -->|only after direct exhaustion| N[service-net mTLS client]
  N -->|attested signer request| K[KMS policy service]
  K -->|one RootProvider boundary| P[Protected root provider]
  P -->|production only: key/sign/epoch/measurement| H[External secure hardware]
  P -. development/reference only .-> Q[AArch64 QEMU Stage-2 Silo]
  K -->|public cert + handle only| N
  N -->|TLS 1.3 mTLS; opaque payload| R[External relay]
  B -->|Noise ciphertext remains end-to-end| R
```

**Phase 0 — contract/reconciliation (board-independent).** Keep `libs/types/src/kms` as the one KMS ABI; define only the necessary protected P-256 TLS-sign operation and certificate/identity metadata, with request transcript/digest validation, opaque key reference, key usage, and typed fail-closed errors. Do not add a parallel Silo wire API or use `SiloHandle` in service-net. Minimal files: KMS types/frame/payload/tests, KMS dispatch/auth tests, `ostd::clients::kms`, ADR/roadmap/guides. Success: malformed, replay/stale-binding, unattested, wrong service, wrong key use, bad digest/scheme all deny; API never contains private bytes. Risk: changing the fixed ABI; append only and retain canonical-frame checks.

**Phase 1 — provider boundary and production-selection gate (board-independent code; production provider hardware-gated).** Evolve the existing `RootProvider` seam—not a second abstraction—so it can open/provision durable identity, report public material/certificate reference, perform P-256 signing, and expose monotonic-policy/measurement/device-binding assessment. Add a build/profile selection rule in `service-kms`: development/reference provider is allowed only in explicitly non-production targets/features; production profile has exactly one external hardware provider and fails compilation/startup if unavailable or if any QEMU/Silo test provider is selectable. Minimal files: KMS `storage/provider.rs`, `storage/root.rs`, `dispatch.rs`, provider-specific module, Cargo/profile/build wiring, tests, docs. Success: runtime/prod selection cannot resolve to TestHooks/QEMU/Silo; unavailable provider produces existing fail-closed status; no provider call returns a secret. Risk: do not infer production capability from `HypervisorCap`, EL2, or QEMU.

**Phase 2 — service-net authorization and KMS lifecycle (board-independent).** Replace the current broker-only binding policy with explicit live service-net instance/generation authorization for TLS identity signing, retaining supervisor-only rotation and fail-closed stale binding. Have service-net register/obtain public status through KMS; broker can receive only non-secret readiness/identity metadata as necessary. Minimal files: KMS `auth.rs`, `dispatch.rs`, `main.rs`, types payloads, service IDs/launch ordering only if required, service-net startup path, KMS tests. Success: forged/no trailer, a broker, arbitrary cell, stale generation, or a direct Silo caller cannot obtain relay signing; live service-net can only invoke the designated TLS signer operation. Risk: current registry snapshot has NET_BROKER and SUPERVISOR only, so adding NET service must remain a direct `sys_lookup_service` identity check, not caller-supplied claims.

**Phase 3 — service-net mTLS client profile (board-independent software completion).** Extend the one existing service-net TLS provider/connection boundary to accept client chain plus a signing callback/reference backed solely by KMS. Preserve server CA/hostname verification and bounded raw transport, but do not expose client key bytes or construct an in-process `p256::SigningKey`. Give net-broker a narrow mTLS relay client through service-net; retain direct Noise first and `NotSupported` if mTLS prerequisites are absent. Minimal files: service-net TLS socket/provider/IPC and tests; ostd TLS client contract; net-broker relay integration and KMS identity bootstrap; no legacy raw relay module. Success: valid test/reference signer produces TLS 1.3 client auth; invalid relay CA/hostname, missing client chain, unavailable signer, denied KMS authorization, stale binding, and direct-path exhaustion all fail closed; no raw TCP/K1 fallback reappears. Risk: embedded-tls 0.19 must actually support required client-auth signing hook; if not, this phase first needs a constrained TLS library/provider decision, not filesystem PEM fallback.

**Phase 4 — reference/QEMU Silo evidence (software-complete only, never production qualification).** If retained, repair the prototype as a reference provider: produce and integrity-check guest artifact, explicit one-time reference initialization, attested KMS-only access instead of `sys_recv(0)`, and provider lifecycle tests. Mark profile/dev-only at compile/startup. Minimal files: Silo service/guest, build artifact path, KMS reference provider adapter, test cell/tests, guide/changelog wording. Success: QEMU proves key remains absent from KMS/net/broker memory representations, signing occurs through only KMS, and all caller/guest/provider failure cases deny. Risk: Stage-2 isolates a guest from normal guest mappings but QEMU is not an immutable device identity, trusted measurement root, anti-rollback counter, or proof against a privileged host/kernel; it cannot clear production gates.

**Phase 5 — external secure-hardware production provider (hardware-required).** Implement the selected hardware provider behind the Phase-1 boundary, including immutable/protected key creation/import policy, device binding, measured boot claim verification, trusted monotonic epoch, certificate enrollment/renewal/revocation, and recovery/rotation. Minimal files depend on selected hardware transport, plus KMS provider adapter, board/provisioning manifest and evidence docs. Success: physical device proves power-cycle persistence, clone/rollback/measurement rejection, non-extractability, service-net-only authorization, cert lifecycle, and audit/recovery behavior. RPi3 is excluded unless boot/control is moved to an independently qualified hardware root; current EL1 RPi3 cannot host the Stage-2 Silo assumption. Risk: secure hardware choices are an operational and attestation architecture decision; KMS must remain hardware-gated rather than silently degrading to Silo/QEMU.

**Phase 6 — end-to-end production qualification (hardware-required).** Provision two hardware-qualified nodes and a managed CA/relay manifest; run ADR-0005’s negative and positive client/relay tests. Success: TLS<1.3, absent/invalid/revoked/mismatched client identities, invalid server trust/hostname, unavailable signer, stale cleanup, and all downgrade attempts fail before registration; successful two-node relay carries opaque Noise ciphertext; physical evidence is separately recorded from host/QEMU tests. Risks: CA compromise, trust-rollover operation, certificate provisioning, and relay resource/duplicate-session handling.

Ownership: `service-kms` owns policy and the single provider boundary; a hardware adapter owns protected-root I/O and qualification; `service-net` owns TLS client execution and is the sole signing caller; `net-broker` owns direct-Noise-first routing and must never own key bytes; `libs/types`/`libs/ostd` own stable IPC and client contracts; kernel owns caller attestation and virtualization capability only. Existing Silo ownership should be narrowed to a development/reference provider or retired from the production path.
